html:
SMTO-LLM-0080 — SMTO doesn't know if the model server action finished

GUID: 05f05716-0978-5379-baad-c7d141be7a31
Slug: local-ai-operation-outcome-unknown
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO lost track of the model server action partway through. It may have finished, may still be running (a download can keep going), or may not have happened. Sending it again could do it twice.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Don't repeat the action yet. In a new message, ask SMTO to list the model servers and installed models on that Gateway. The list shows whether the server started or stopped, or the model downloaded or was removed.
  2. If you were downloading a large model, wait a few minutes and check the installed models list again. SMTO stops watching a download after five minutes, but the model server may keep downloading.
  3. If the lists show a server with unknown status, ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check it there. SMTO won't act on a server it can't prove it controls, so someone on that computer must confirm its state.
  4. Only if the lists show the action did not happen, ask SMTO to do it again. Checking first avoids two copies of a server or a second download.

What success looks like

  • The model servers and installed models on that Gateway show the result you wanted, either from the first attempt or from a single new one.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't delete SMTO's saved model server records to clear this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Local AI manager has no conclusive result for a mutation (start, stop, restart, pull or remove) after a transport/process error, a lost or overlong pull stream, an unreadable saved runtimes record, a full receipt journal, or an existing runtime of unknown ownership.

What this means

  • The management layer lacks conclusive completion evidence after possible mutation, unreadable saved state or an exhausted receipt bound; repeating the request can duplicate effects. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The management layer lacks conclusive completion evidence after possible mutation, unreadable saved state or an exhausted receipt bound; repeating the request can duplicate effects.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the original execution ID, exact runtime ownership, model inventory and activation revisions; a healthy endpoint alone cannot settle the original action.

How to fix it

  • Do not replay the mutation. Inspect local_ai.runtimes, local_ai.runtime and local_ai.models on the profile's Gateway (and the provider's own log/process list) to determine the exact outcome; if the Gateway's local_ai runtimes.json could not be read or holds 1,024 receipts, resolve that with the Gateway operator before any new mutation.
  • Do not replay the mutation. Reconcile its exact operation and target with the Gateway/provider owner first.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not replay the mutation. Reconcile its exact operation and target with the Gateway/provider owner first.

How to verify the fix

  • Authoritative runtime, model or configuration state and the original receipt establish what happened.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
